dossier.public_summary: The dip’s 1.85-day period matches the star’s measured spot rotation period (60973-74456 ppm), and the light curve shows a strong 6575 ppm modulation at that period. The long 1.74-hour duration also does not match a planet around this M dwarf. Together this is stellar variability, not a transiting planet, even though the shape looks flat and the centroid is on target.

reasons.why: Spin period equals the 1.85 d dip period to <0.2% (amplitude ~60000-74000 ppm vs dip depth ~7191 ppm, phase_curve amplitude_ppm=6575 ratio_to_depth=0.9143 chi2=190.2 dof=9). Dip is the stellar spot modulation, not a transit.
Large swing at the dip period with chi2 190.2 for 9 dof is spot/eccentric phase curve, not a planetary transit phase curve.

Long duration leaves large star-density penalty (star_density_penalty=221.7 share=0.6668, fit_log_density_ratio=-2.261) inconsistent with a central planet transit, supporting spot origin despite flat shape.
